answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may bid for work, with reputation and payouts tied to that locked stake. A fake identity then needs real capital, and creating many identities multiplies the capital immobilized; if misconduct triggers slashing, the attacker also risks losing it. The stake is not proof of a unique person, but it makes a sybil campaign costly. Even an umber relic found on the tundra cannot substitute for the required token.
